steps.title: Base on fixture: chassis with pressed-in door nuts, rear under-base dam
Push in feet (fixture holds base over clearance holes)
Set coil standoffs
Standoff screws from below
native-21 male-female standoffs threaded into the base
PE chassis hardware
Controller snap-in supports pushed into the base
SELV controller board (under the fascia)
EMI module stand: tabs through base slots, twisted (top PEM nuts pre-clinched)
EMI stand M3 screw from above into the tapped base (R32)
D-22 inlet EMI module onto its stand
EMI case PE braid: module rear stud to S1 (hand, R32)
Inlet bulkhead with the EC11 and window gasket (fixed, R32 study 05)
Bulkhead M4 screws from below
Blower on its two isolating spacers, inlet down over the base field (R32 study 02)
native-21 subassembly (board, components; insulator layer, spreader bar, FR-4 strip and comb clamp the sink to the FET/BR1 row)
native-21 top screws
PS3 blower-supply subassembly (bench: IRM-60 screwed to its bracket, both blocks wired), lowered beside native-21 before the push hood's F2 duct closes over its rear end (R41)
Sink cradle with its pad slid in under the sink from behind, lip into the fin channel (R33 study 07); floats in its Y slot
Cradle M3 screw from above through the slot, after the comb is torqued (R33 study 04)
Sink thermal cutoff
Push hood with its F2 bleed duct, and the exhaust plenum (R32 study 02)
Push-hood and plenum-wall M3 screws from above into the tapped base
Nomex over the sink top (coil plenum)
Plug native-21 J3 and J4 mates

PS3 J11 tie anchor (R42): lowered from above outboard of native-21, its fin over the plugged J11 housing (3 mm clear), two M3 screws into the base nuts; the mains lead is routed beside its fin afterwards and tied to it

J13 barrier (R43): lowered from above into the 6.4 mm strip between the controller's edge and native-21's board edge, after the controller, native-21 and its J11 mate; the two snap tabs push through the base floor slots and the barbs catch under the floor; the DC pair is routed and tied to it afterwards
Harness lane brackets and mains anchor: tabs through base slots, twisted
Route harness (hand, flexible; under the carrier channel, before the coil goes in)

Coil and sensor subassembly (SELV tray hung under the carrier, R32; coil leads with their crimped ring lugs). Hold ~50 mm above the seat, torque the J2/J5 M4 nuts through the open gap, then lower (lead slack loop)
Coil carrier top screws
Coil-ear M3 screws from above into the tapped carrier (R33: replaces the PEEK rim clips)

Sink PE bond ends (hand, after the coil drop: the bolt head sits 7.5 mm over the Nomex barrier corner and would block the barrier lowering; carrier is open at X>130 for access): ear lug on the M4 through-bolt stack, toothed washers on masked faces, nyloc 1.2 N m; base-stud lug + toothed washers + M4 nut (PEM FHA-M4-12 pressed in with the base)
Sensor cartridge: drop through the bayonet notches, turn 60°
steps.path: bayonet: drop 60 mm with lugs in notches, then turn 60°

Cover screws from below
Door subassembly (door, cassette, hook studs and brackets, gasket)
Door screws from below
Push on knob

scope:
Replay the R14 assembly sequence and sweep each step's insertion path.

The product is built top-down on the base: every step moves a part or a bench
subassembly along a stated path into its installed position. Each sampled pose
is checked against everything installed in earlier steps. This is a rigid,
sampled screen (5 mm steps far out, 1 mm within 20 mm of seat, plus 0.5 mm).

Not modelled: hand-routed flexible harness (installed without a sweep), the
deformation of snap-in and compressible parts (listed as compliant pairs),
and two-piece screw-and-nut sets, which are placed (their screw and nut arrive
from opposite sides). Tool reach is outside this check.
